text.arabic_uthmani: يَوْمَ لَا يُغْنِى عَنْهُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ

words.gloss_range: accusative temporal adverb, locally carrying forward the prior Day-frame and setting the time of both denials
words.root_gloss_range: day, time, appointed moment, or decisive reckoning; here narrowed to the reckoning Day already introduced at 52:45
words.prose: {{ar:يَوْمَ}} ({{tr:yawma}}) does not open a detached new scene. Its accusative temporal form carries forward the prior possessed Day-expression of 52:45, then makes that same Day the operating frame in which their plot fails and they are not helped. The suffixless form shifts from a Day assigned to them to an impersonal reckoning frame, while the audible final vowel keeps the word dependent as a time-adverb. Same-surah recurrences at 52:9 and 52:13 make this another entry in the surah's Day-sequence, and the frame stretches to the final no-help verdict.

topics.headline: prior Day carried into this ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that {{ar:يَوْمَ}} ({{tr:yawma}}) continues the Day named in 52:45 rather than starting an unrelated sentence.
topics.reason: The bundle licenses {{ar:يَوْمَ}} ({{tr:yawma}}) as an accusative temporal adverb appositive to, or continuing, the prior Day expression at 52:45.

topics.headline: one temporal frame holds both denials
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both the failed plotting and the no-help verdict happen inside one appointed temporal frame.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes word 1 the temporal setting for the first negated clause, while coordination ties the second negated clause into the same ayah movement.

topics.headline: common day word narrowed to reckoning
topics.reader_payoff: The common day word is heard here as a decisive reckoning marker because the following clauses define it by failed resources and absent rescue.
topics.reason: The root is broad and frequent, so the reckoning sense is not automatic from the root alone; it is selected locally by 52:45 and the double denial.

topics.headline: suffixless dependent time word
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees the word as a dependent time-frame, no longer a possessed Day-expression.
topics.reason: The accusative form and loss of the prior suffix are visible local form facts.

topics.headline: Day-frame reaches zero benefit and no help
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the Day not as a date but as the frame where zero benefit and no help are jointly exposed.
topics.reason: The row-level co-occurrence claims are retained as local structural payoff because this ayah actually contains the Day-frame, the zero-minimizer, and the final no-help verb.

words.gloss_range: first negative particle, scoping over the imperfect availing verb and through the zero-minimizer

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the zero-minimizer at the end of the first denial

words.prose: The first {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:la}}) is the polarity switch for the first clause. It negates the imperfect {{ar:يُغْنِى}} ({{tr:yughni}}) and keeps its force through {{ar:شَيْـًۭٔا}} ({{tr:shay'an}}), so the clause denies any future availing down to the smallest possible measure. It also begins the first half of the later {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:la}}) ... {{ar:وَلَا}} ({{tr:wa-la}}) pattern, making the first denial expect a coordinated second denial.

topics.headline: first negation reaches the zero endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:la}}) does not merely negate a verb; it drives the denial all the way to no benefit whatsoever.
topics.reason: The clause structure licenses negation over the imperfect verb with the indefinite minimizer completing the scope.

topics.headline: first arm of a paired denial
topics.reader_payoff: The repeated negator lets the reader hear two coordinated exclusions rather than two unrelated negative statements.
topics.reason: The first negative particle is matched by the second negative particle after the conjunction, producing a locally visible paired frame.

words.gloss_range: negated Form IV imperfect: avail, suffice, or make unnecessary, here intransitive with an {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:an}})-complement and a zero-minimizer
words.root_gloss_range: sufficiency, richness, being free of need, and causing sufficiency; here the active branch is failed availing or sufficing on behalf of the group

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the prepositional complement marking the affected group
the zero-minimizer of the availing clause

words.prose: {{ar:يُغْنِى}} ({{tr:yughni}}) tests whether their plot can suffice for them, stand in for protection, or produce any availing result, and the surrounding negation says it cannot. The local frame is not bare richness: the Form IV verb is used with {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:anhum}}) and {{ar:شَيْـًۭٔا}} ({{tr:shay'an}}), so the imagined substitute-benefit is measured against zero. The first predicate is active and dynamic before the ayah turns to the passive no-help ending. The same non-availing pattern appears with other failed resources at 3:10, 3:116, and 58:17; here the failed resource is their own plotting. The broader divine self-sufficiency register of the root remains background only, while the local sense is failed sufficiency.

topics.headline: failed sufficiency tested to zero
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the verb asks whether their scheme can substitute for real protection, not merely whether it is useful in a vague way.
topics.reason: The local verb instance is Form IV with an {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:an}})-complement and no direct object, and the minimizer supplies the zero endpoint.

topics.headline: active failed action before passive no-help
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah first stages an action-potential being tested before it states their settled unsupported condition.
topics.reason: The first predicate is an active imperfect verb, while the final predicate is passive and embedded in a nominal clause.

topics.headline: non-availing formula applied to plotting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a Quranic non-availing formula, but with plotting inserted as the failed resource in this ayah.
topics.reason: The supplied recurrence rows give concrete parallels at 3:10, 3:116, and 58:17, and the local wording contains the same negated availing plus minimizer pattern.

topics.headline: imperfect form lets benefit be denied as potential
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the possible availing stretch forward before the clause cuts it down to nothing.
topics.reason: The imperfect morphology and recitational observations are local to the displayed verb and its immediate clause.

topics.headline: root theology kept as background
topics.reader_payoff: The broader root field sharpens the contrast between true sufficiency and failed human self-protection, while local grammar selects failed availing.
topics.reason: The row's theological polarity is not rejected, but the local Form IV frame does not name the divine epithet; it narrows the payoff to failed sufficiency.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus third-person plural suffix, marking the affected party for whom the failed availing would have operated

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: their plot as the delayed subject
the same group as final independent topic

words.prose: {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:anhum}}) routes the failed availing toward the very people it cannot protect. After {{ar:يُغْنِى}} ({{tr:yughni}}), the preposition marks the party on whose behalf the benefit would need to work, while the suffix keeps the same group from 52:45 in view. Its placement between the verb and {{ar:كَيْدُهُمْ}} ({{tr:kayduhum}}) delays the subject, so the endangered people are heard before the failed instrument is named. The repeated {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) sound ties beneficiary, possessor, and final topic into one chain.

topics.headline: affected party marked through the preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees benefit pictured as something that would have to work on their behalf, and the clause says it does not reach them.
topics.reason: The attachment data force the prepositional complement as governed by the availing verb.

topics.headline: same group carried by suffix
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same opponents through affected beneficiary, plot-owner, and final explicit subject.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence identifies the suffix as the continuing third-person plural group.

topics.headline: prepositional hinge delays the failed instrument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader first hears whom the failure concerns, then discovers that the failed candidate is their own plot.
topics.reason: The local order places the prepositional phrase between the verb and its nominative subject.

words.gloss_range: their scheming, plot, or calculated stratagem, functioning as the nominative subject of the failed availing verb
words.root_gloss_range: plotting, stratagem, hidden maneuver, and broader counter-plotting range; local sense is their owned oppositional scheme tested and nullified
words.prose: {{ar:كَيْدُهُمْ}} ({{tr:kayduhum}}) is the grammatical subject that finally names what cannot avail: their own calculated scheme. The verbal noun turns plotting itself into the thing put on trial, while the attached suffix makes it possessively definite and self-generated. The word answers the earlier plotting language of 52:42; what was raised there as an intended plot returns here as {{ar:كَيْدُهُمْ}} ({{tr:kayduhum}}), the very subject of the non-availing verdict. A secondary expulsion image in the root can sharpen the movement from concealed design to exposed futility, but it remains subordinate to the local sense of plotting. Wider plotting scenes such as 12:5, 12:28, 12:50, and 12:76 show the root's narrative range, while this ayah's local contrast is between self-generated strategy and denied external help.

topics.headline: plotting itself becomes the tested subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the scheme itself, not merely the plotters, placed in the subject slot and judged ineffective.
topics.reason: The noun instance and attachment evidence identify the verbal noun as the nominative subject of the availing verb.

topics.headline: their own identifiable scheme fails
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the failure belongs to their own owned production, not to an anonymous plot or external trap.
topics.reason: The construct noun with suffix binds the plot to the continuing third-person plural group.

topics.headline: calculated plotting with exposed futility
topics.reader_payoff: The word preserves calculated hidden planning, while the local context makes that planning oppositional and futile.
topics.reason: The local sense is stratagem; secondary physical or morally neutral branches are retained only as color where the negated outcome and 52:42 charge the plot negatively.

topics.headline: 52:42 plotting question receives its verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 52:46 answer the earlier question about plotting in 52:42 by declaring that very plotting useless.
topics.reason: The supplied CRITICAL rows give the concrete same-surah recurrence at 52:42, and the local noun is the failed subject of the availing verb.

topics.headline: internal strategy paired against external help
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah close both survival routes: what they generate internally and what might arrive externally.
topics.reason: The local sequence contains their plot in the first denial and the passive help verb in the second denial.

topics.headline: broader plotting field kept as apparatus
topics.reader_payoff: The wider root field shows that plotting is not weak by definition; the failure here comes from these agents and this Day-frame.
topics.reason: Distant plotting scenes and divine-human contrasts are useful background, but they do not override the local same-surah echo and syntactic subject role.

topics.headline: suffix sound binds roles together
topics.reader_payoff: The repeated suffix sound lets the same group be heard as beneficiaries, owners of the plot, and the final topic.
topics.reason: The local sequence repeats the third-person plural sound in the prepositional suffix, possessive suffix, and independent pronoun.

words.gloss_range: anything, any thing, or any amount; here an indefinite accusative minimizer under negation
words.root_gloss_range: thing, entity, object, or amount at the broadest level; locally it marks the smallest conceivable benefit denied

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the first negative particle governing the minimizer

words.prose: {{ar:شَيْـًۭٔا}} ({{tr:shay'an}}) is the zero endpoint of the first denial. Whether parsed as a direct object or as an accusative intensifier, it converges on the same payoff: their plot produces no object of benefit and helps in no manner at all. Its indefiniteness under {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:la}}) turns the broadest thing-word into a universal minimizer. The formula of negated availing plus {{ar:شَيْـًۭٔا}} ({{tr:shay'an}}) appears at 3:10, 3:116, 4:123, 58:17, and 111:2; 52:46 applies that absolute futility pattern to plotting. The hamza and tanwin give the clause-final minimizer an audible arrest and unbounded finish before the conjunction moves to the second denial.

topics.headline: object or intensifier both reach total zero
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the grammatical ambiguity strengthens rather than weakens the total-zero reading.
topics.reason: The bundle permits accusative object or specification/intensifier analysis, and both readings support total denial.

topics.headline: indefinite thing-word universalizes the denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that no category or amount of benefit is left outside the negation.
topics.reason: The noun is indefinite and under negation, with the broad thing-root locally functioning as the minimum conceivable unit.

topics.headline: formulaic non-availing endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a recurring absolute-futility formula and sees plotting as the item inserted into it here.
topics.reason: The row gives concrete formula parallels, and the local clause contains the same negated availing plus minimizer structure.

topics.headline: first clause lands before the second denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first denial complete its own architecture before the ayah adds the second denial.
topics.reason: The sequence contains negator, predicate, beneficiary, subject, and minimizer before the conjunction.

topics.headline: hamza and tanwin make the endpoint audible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the zero-benefit word close with both a catch and indefinite breadth.
topics.reason: The sound observations are tied to the local spelling and case ending of the clause-final noun.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction, here launching the second arm of a paired negation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the following negative particle in the coordinated connector

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the pivot after the first denial has reached zero. Joined with the following {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:la}}), it begins the second arm of the paired negation and links a verbal failure clause to a nominal no-help clause. The conjunction is additive rather than explanatory: their internal strategy has already failed, and now the separate route of external help is denied. Its tight sound and written connection with {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:la}}) make coordination and negation arrive together.

topics.headline: conjunction launches the second denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the conjunction as the hinge that turns one completed negation into a paired no-route structure.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the second negated clause with the first and is locally bound to the following negative particle.

topics.headline: bridge from dynamic failure to static state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammar shift from failed action to settled helplessness while the conjunction keeps both clauses joined.
topics.reason: The first coordinated unit is verbal and the second is nominal with an explicit pronoun subject.

topics.headline: another denied resource category is added
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the first denial was not the whole statement; a second, complementary survival route is closed.
topics.reason: The conjunction links the denial of their plot's benefit with the denial of being helped.

topics.headline: connector and negator are tightly joined
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the second denial begin as one tight connector-negator unit.
topics.reason: The recitational observation is tied to the local boundary between the conjunction and the following negative particle.

words.gloss_range: second negative particle, scoping over a nominal topic-comment clause with a passive predicate
words.prose: The second {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:la}}) completes the paired negative frame. Unlike the first {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:la}}), it negates a topic-comment structure, {{ar:هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ}} ({{tr:hum yunsaruna}}), so the denial lands on their state of not being helped, not only on an action failing to occur. Bound into {{ar:وَلَا}} ({{tr:wa-la}}), it closes the neither-nor architecture: no benefit from their plot and no help reaching them. Its repetition also gives the ayah an audible negative cadence.

topics.headline: second negation freezes no-help as state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second denial describes their unsupported condition, not just the failure of a helper's action.
topics.reason: The second negative particle precedes an explicit pronoun plus passive predicate, creating a nominal predication under negation.

topics.headline: second arm closes the paired denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah complete an exhaustive pair: neither internal strategy nor external support remains.
topics.reason: The second negative particle is coordinated with the first through the conjunction and governs the second denied resource category.

topics.headline: written and sounded reprise of negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees and hears the second denial as a reprise of the first, not as a stray appended clause.
topics.reason: The particle is visually joined to the conjunction and repeats the earlier negative particle.

words.gloss_range: independent third-person plural pronoun, fronted as the topic of the final no-help clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the earlier prepositional suffix for the same group
the earlier possessive noun naming their plot

words.prose: {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) gives the people their own syntactic slot before the passive verb. Because {{ar:يُنصَرُونَ}} ({{tr:yunsaruna}}) already carries plural agreement, the independent pronoun is not needed merely to mark person; it foregrounds them as the topic of helplessness. The same referents have already appeared as suffixes in {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:anhum}}) and {{ar:كَيْدُهُمْ}} ({{tr:kayduhum}}), but here they stand detached, and the nasal transition into {{ar:يُنصَرُونَ}} ({{tr:yunsaruna}}) carries the topic into its predicate. That shift moves the ayah from their act to their persons: failed strategy becomes abandoned agents, and the boundary scene from 52:45 culminates with them isolated inside the Day's no-help condition.

topics.headline: independent pronoun foregrounds them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the people themselves are foregrounded before the no-help predicate lands.
topics.reason: The independent pronoun functions as the fronted nominal subject of the final predicate.

topics.headline: embedded referents become explicit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same group moving from attached suffixes into an independent final topic.
topics.reason: The suffixes in the earlier words and the independent pronoun are all resolved to the same third-person plural group.

topics.headline: failed act escalates to abandoned persons
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the movement from the failure of their act to the exposure of them as unsupported persons.
topics.reason: The ayah moves from a possessive noun naming their plot to an independent pronoun naming them before the passive no-help verb.

topics.headline: prior referents isolated in the final clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees those left in the prior boundary scene become the explicit subjects of no help.
topics.reason: The cross-reference evidence keeps the third-person plural group continuous from the prior ayah into this final nominal clause.

topics.headline: pronoun sound binds to the passive predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the pronoun carried into the final passive verb rather than left as an isolated topic.
topics.reason: The sound observation is local to the transition from the independent pronoun into the following passive verb.

words.gloss_range: they are helped, supported, rescued, or granted aid; locally negated as a passive final predicate with no named helper
words.root_gloss_range: help, support, victory, rescue, and aid; here the passive imperfect denies received support or rescue while leaving the helper slot unnamed

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the fronted pronoun before the passive predicate

words.prose: {{ar:يُنصَرُونَ}} ({{tr:yunsaruna}}) closes the ayah by denying received help. As a passive predicate after {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}), it says they are not helped, with the helper left unnamed rather than supplied as an Arabic-side referent. That passivity matters: the first half denies what their own plot can generate, and the last word denies what could be granted to them from outside. The root's support field includes help, rescue, and victory, so the denial is broader than battlefield victory alone. Formulaic no-help settings such as 2:48, 2:123, and 44:41 confirm the judgment-day register, while the contrast with promised divine help at 110:1 remains a theological backdrop, not a named agent here. The final position, long plural ending, and heavier consonantal texture make no-help the ayah's closing sound, answering the boundary of being left in 52:45 and pressing toward the punishment statement in 52:47.

topics.headline: passive predicate leaves helper unnamed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word foregrounds their unsupported state while leaving the possible helper slot empty.
topics.reason: The verb is passive, functions as the predicate of the fronted pronoun, and has no expressed helper-agent.

topics.headline: wide support field denied without naming agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears help, support, victory, and rescue denied, while local grammar prevents naming a specific helper-agent.
topics.reason: The root field is broad, but the passive construction leaves the agent unexpressed, so divine withdrawal can be backdrop rather than an inserted subject.

topics.headline: self-generated plot and received help both fail
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the two halves are not redundant: one denies what they produce, the other denies what can be given to them.
topics.reason: The first clause has their plot as active subject, while the final predicate makes them passive recipients of help that never arrives.

topics.headline: final clause states settled unsupportedness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees no-help presented as their condition, not merely as one failed episode.
topics.reason: The final unit is a negated nominal clause with a passive predicate after an explicit pronoun.

topics.headline: judgment-day no-help formula field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the final verb as part of a judgment-day no-help field while keeping 52:46's local passive grammar in control.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply concrete parallels at 2:48, 2:123, 44:41, and 110:1; they are useful formulaic backdrop but not replacements for the local predicate.

topics.headline: last word makes no-help the closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah land on the prolonged absence of help.
topics.reason: The no-help verb is the terminal word and carries the plural ending that supplies the audible closure.

topics.headline: no-help verdict answers boundary and points forward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final no-help verdict answer the earlier withdrawal frame and leave punishment as what remains.
topics.reason: The boundary rows connect 52:45 to the no-help verdict and point forward to the punishment language in 52:47.

topics.headline: passive plural form encodes received aid
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the people grammatically encoded as receivers of aid that never occurs, not as active helpers or self-rescuers.
topics.reason: The local form is passive with no object and no expressed agent; the comparison to reflexive self-help is retained as form specificity.

topics.headline: consonantal texture thickens the ending
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final support-denial as a weighty acoustic endpoint.
topics.reason: The sound row is local to the final word and remains a small recitational payoff.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired clauses negate what their possessed plot can do and whether they themselves receive aid; the indefinite shay'an sits inside the first negation.
baseline_models.mechanism: The verse dismantles two escape channels rather than reporting one failed tactic. Internally controlled stratagem cannot suffice, benefit, or substitute for what is needed, while externally supplied aid cannot make them prevail. Shay'an drives the first failure toward a zero remainder.

activation_trace.role: Sufficing, benefiting, or standing in for another casts the possessed plot as an instrument expected to replace what is needed; negation removes that function.
Plotting and stratagem supply the internally controlled means whose efficacy is denied.
A knowable or reportable entity gives the indefinite accusative exhaustive scope: no residual benefit registers.
Aid that makes its recipient prevail supplies the separate external rescue channel also negated.

changed_reading.before: Their plan fails and nobody helps them.
changed_reading.after: Both self-produced leverage and other-produced leverage are independently zeroed; neither the plot nor a patron can substitute for what the event requires.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Yawm opens the verse and governs both failures.
baseline_models.mechanism: The day can be read as a severe occurrence rather than a neutral calendar label. It names a regime change in which forceful management no longer converts into sufficiency and aid no longer converts into prevalence.

activation_trace.role: The event-day or severe occasion turns the temporal noun into the operative crisis itself.
Availing and standing-in define the capacity that the event regime switches off.
Forceful handling broadens the lost capacity beyond secret plotting to strenuous management.
Prevailing aid is the second capacity unavailable inside that regime.

changed_reading.before: At a future date their scheme will stop working.
changed_reading.after: They enter an event whose conditions deactivate both strenuous agency and outside support at once.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Kayduhum is the grammatical subject of la yughni, followed by shay'an.
baseline_models.mechanism: Keeping the forceful-handling branch live makes the line about failed conversion of effort, not only defeated cunning. Their strenuous treatment of the situation yields no unit of useful result.

activation_trace.role: Benefit and sufficiency provide the expected output of effort and mark its absence.
Forceful handling supplies labor, pressure, and active struggle without requiring covert intrigue.
The general knowable thing lets the negation measure the output at nothing whatsoever.

changed_reading.before: A cunning design is defeated by a stronger design.
changed_reading.after: The verse can also describe an input-output collapse: maximal handling produces no convertible benefit at all.

context_deltas.mechanism: The sequence supplies a public containment campaign: mark the messenger as occult expert, mentally covered, or poet; wait for time to remove him; attribute invented speech; then fail the challenge to produce a truthful analogue. Kayd becomes narrative classification plus attrition, not merely a hidden physical plot.

activation_trace.role: A soothsayer claiming hidden reports supplies the first delegitimizing label.
Covering the intellect with madness supplies a second label that blocks reception of the message.
Poetry and poet recategorize revelation as human literary performance.
Waiting and watching supply attrition as the campaign's temporal mechanism.
Attributing speech that did not occur supplies the fabrication charge.
Renewed speech or report supplies the demanded counterproduction.
Similarity makes a rival utterance the proposed test of their classification.
Truthful speech makes successful counterproduction the condition their charge must meet.
Stratagem anchors the coordinated labels, waiting, and counter-speech back in the focus.
Failure to avail states that the containment campaign cannot substitute a rival account for the message.

changed_reading.before: Their plot is an unspecified covert conspiracy.
changed_reading.after: Their plot can include a visible narrative campaign that labels, waits out, and tries to replace the message, yet cannot make the replacement hold.

context_deltas.mechanism: The creation questions place the same thing-root at the boundary between no supplied origin and creative agency. This activates a productive-causality reading of the focus: agents who neither originate themselves nor the world cannot make their strenuous plan bring even one operative result into being.

activation_trace.role: Bringing creation into being supplies the productive power under interrogation.
Otherness, exception, and negation open the impossible option of origin without a supplied cause.

The repeated thing-root measures the plan's productive yield at not one entity or result.

summary.what_was_special: The packet activated rhetorical, ontological, infrastructural, economic, social, temporal, perceptual, and counteragential mechanisms without forcing them into one final interpretation; somatic, acoustic, and hydrological branches remain explicitly contained as live resonances.
remaining_uncertainties: The imposed labels may be independent objections rather than one coordinated narrative campaign.
The vertical access model depends on reading adjacent interrogatives as one resource-information-warrant stack.
The nearer punishment in 52:47 need not imply gradual erosion of strategic efficacy.
The three outliers are branch-backed resonances, not claims about the primary syntax or lexical sense of the focus words.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da güçlü emek ve gayret bileşenini taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal çabayı bir şeyi ele alıp işleme ilişkisi içinde kurar; komşu dalın çekirdeği ise çabanın kendisidir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Aldatma veya gizli amaç olmaksızın bir şeyi yoğun çabayla ele almayı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Birini yönlendirmek ya da alt etmek için gizli ve dolaylı bir düzen kurmayı gerektirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da bir amaca yönelik, tasarlanmış bir uğraş bulunabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın çekirdeği yoğun işlemedir; komşu dalın çekirdeği ise bir başkasını dolaylı yollarla etkilemeye yönelik düzen kurmadır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, birini dolaylı yollarla etkilemek için düzen kurma çekirdeğini; karşılıklı düzen kurma, kötülük isteme, adım adım çekme ve cezaya götüren süre tanıma kullanımlarıyla birlikte açıkça destekler. Bu düzen hem kötü hem de yerinde görülen amaçlarla kurulabilir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek dolaylı ve tasarlanmış yönlendirmedir; yoğun uğraşma tek başına bu anlamı oluşturmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın ad ve eylem biçimlerindeki gizli düzen anlamı, belirli söz öbeklerinde kötülük isteme veya cezaya götüren erteleme olarak gerçekleşen özel kullanımlardan ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Birini yönlendirmek, yanıltmak ya da alt etmek amacıyla açık edilmeyen, dolaylı bir düzen kurmaktır. Bağlama göre bu düzen övülebilir veya yerilebilir; karşılıklı çekişme, kötülük tasarlama ve cezaya götüren süre tanıma biçimlerinde gerçekleşebilir.

facets.statement: Bir kişi ya da taraf, amacına ulaşmak için dolaylı ve önceden tasarlanmış bir düzen kurar.
İki taraf birbirini alt etmek amacıyla karşılıklı olarak düzen kurabilir.
Belirli bir söz içinde, hedefe kötülük etmeye yönelik kesin niyeti anlatır.
Başka bir özel kullanımda, kişiye sonunda cezaya varacak biçimde süre tanıyıp onu adım adım sonuca çekmeyi anlatır.
Kurulan düzen amacına ve sonucuna göre kötülenebileceği gibi yerinde de görülebilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kaynak anlatımı, dolaylı düzen kurma çekirdeğini paylaşır; bunun karşılıklı yapılabileceğini, kötü ya da yerinde amaç taşıyabileceğini ve bazı bağlamlarda adım adım çekme, kötülük isteme veya cezaya götüren erteleme olarak yorumlandığını belirtir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Birini yönlendirme, yanıltma veya alt etme amacıyla tasarlanan genel çekirdeği karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Tasarlamayı, dolaylılığı ve bir başkasını etkilemeye yönelik düzen kurmayı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Düzenin karşı tarafı yanıltma veya zarara uğratma amacı açık olduğunda doğal bir eylem karşılığıdır.

error_profile.preserves: Gizli düzeni ve bir hedefe yönelmeyi korur.
error_profile.loses: Yerinde görülebilen veya doğrudan zarar amacı taşımayan düzenleri dışarıda bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İki tarafın birbirini alt etmek için karşılıklı olarak gizli planlar kurduğu kullanımda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Karşılıklılığı, tasarlamayı ve üstün gelme amacını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Süre vermenin görünürde rahatlık sağladığı, fakat kişiyi sonunda cezaya yaklaştırdığı özel söz bağlamına uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Ertelemeyi, aşamalı ilerleyişi ve ceza sonucunu birlikte korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Cezaya götüren süre tanıma ve kötülük isteme gibi özel gerçekleşmeleri içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Düşmanlık, çekişme ve haklı ya da haksız karşı koyma alanına açıkça uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da karşı tarafı dolaylı yollarla alt etmeye yönelik düzen kurmayı kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Gizli niyetin dışarıya ters bir görünüş verilmeden de kurulabildiği daha geniş düzen alanını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir şeyi gösterirken başka bir şeyi isteme ve görünüşle niyeti ayırma kalıbına bağlıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da gerçek amaç saklanarak karşı tarafın algısı yönlendirilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal her türlü dolaylı düzeni kapsar; komşu dal özellikle söylenen veya gösterilen ile istenen arasındaki karşıtlığa dayanır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, kişinin canını vermekte oluşunu ve ölümün son aşamasından geçmesini anlatan kalıplaşmış kullanımı destekler. Burada çekirdek, genel bir zorluk değil, ölüm sırasında canın çıkış sürecidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam yalnız kişiyle ve can verme bağlamıyla kurulan söz öbeğine bağlıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnız canla kurulan söz öbeğini karşılar; yalın biçime genel ölme veya zorluk anlamı yüklemez.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin ölümün son aşamasında can çekişmesi ve canını vermek üzere olmasıdır.

facets.statement: Kişi ölümün son aşamasında canını vermekte ve yaşamı bedenden ayrılmaktadır.
Kaynak anlatımları aynı süreci canı verme ve ölümün son sıkıntısından geçme yönleriyle ifade eder.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, kalıbı can çekişme ve canını verme süreci üzerinde birleştirir; anlatım farkı bu son aşamanın hangi yönünün öne çıkarıldığıyla ilgilidir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yalnız ölümün son aşamasındaki kişi için kullanılan söz öbeğinin bütün çekirdeğini karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Ölümün son aşamasını, çekişmeyi ve can verme sonucuna yaklaşmayı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişinin ölümün son aşamasında bulunduğu bağlamda doğal ve kısa bir metin içi karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Kişinin ölmek üzere oluşunu ve son aşamadaki sıkıntılı süreci korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: can çekişmek ve canını vermek üzere olmak

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Canın verilmesini belirli bir söz öbeği içinde süreç olarak anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Ölüm sırasındaki çekişme ve son nefes belirtilerini daha doğrudan öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da ölümün hemen öncesindeki can çekişme sürecini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal can verme yönünü kalıba bağlı biçimde kurar; komşu dal ölüm sırasındaki dışa vuran çekişmeyi daha belirginleştirir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Canın çıkışını süren bir can çekişme ve can verme olayı olarak anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Kişinin yaşamdan kalan en son soluğa ulaştığı durumu bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal ölümden hemen önceki son yaşam evresine aittir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal can verme sürecini, komşu dal ise bu sürecin sonunda kalan son soluk durumunu öne çıkarır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Ölmekte olan kişinin yaşadığı can çekişme sürecini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Ölümü, yaşam gücünün alınması veya kişinin alınmış olması sonucu üzerinden kurar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da yaşamın sona ermesini ve canın bedenden ayrılmasını konu edinir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal ölmekte olan kişinin sürecine, komşu dal ise ölümün yaşamın alınması olarak kavranmasına odaklanır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, sefere çıkanların savaşla karşılaşıp karşılaşmadığını bildiren belirli bir kalıpta sözcüğün doğrudan savaş anlamına geldiğini gösterir. Bu, genel gizli düzen anlamıyla birleştirilmemelidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam, savaşla karşılaşmayı bildiren olumsuz söz kalıbına bağlıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnız savaşla karşılaşmama söz kalıbını kapsar ve yalın biçime genel savaş anlamı vermez.

concept_map.definition: Sefere ya da çatışmaya çıkan birinin savaşla karşılaşmamasını bildiren kalıpta, karşılaşılması beklenen savaş veya çarpışmadır.

facets.statement: Söz kalıbındaki nesne, yola çıkanların karşılaşmadığı savaş veya silahlı çatışmadır.
Tipik kullanım, sefere çıkıp hiçbir savaşla karşılaşmama durumunu bildirir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, belirli olumsuz karşılaşma kalıbında sözcüğün savaş veya çarpışma anlamına geldiğinde birleşir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sefere çıkan birinin savaşla karşılaşmadığını bildiren kalıba bağlı anlamı eksiksiz karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Savaş anlamını, karşılaşma ilişkisini ve olumsuz kalıp sınırını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Özne sefere veya çatışma alanına çıkmışken hiçbir savaş görmediğini anlatan cümlede doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Savaş olayını ve onunla karşılaşılmamasını birlikte korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Savaş anlamını yalnız karşılaşmama bildiren belirli söz kalıbında taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Savaşı, savaşmayı, düşmanlığı ve bunlarla ilgili kişi ve yerleri daha geniş biçimde kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalın ortak çekirdeğinde savaş ve silahlı çatışma bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal kalıba bağlı ve dar bir savaş karşılığıdır; komşu dal savaş alanını yalın ve daha geniş bir söz varlığıyla kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Savaşın gerçekleşmediği karşılaşma bağlamında savaş kavramını adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Savaşın kızışmasını, tarafların çarpışmasını ve savaşçı kargaşayı öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da savaş ve karşı karşıya gelen taraflar alanındadır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal karşılaşılması mümkün genel savaşı adlandırır; komşu dal fiilen başlayan ve kızışan çarpışmayı anlatır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Savaşın kendisini, onunla karşılaşmama kalıbında nesne olarak kurar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Savaş içindeki çarpışma anını ve bir topluluğun düşmana saldırmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal savaş alanındaki silahlı karşılaşmayı konu edinir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal genel savaş kavramını kalıba bağlı olarak verir; komşu dal savaş içindeki saldırı ve karşılıklı çarpışma olayına yönelir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, genel bir seslenmeyi değil, karganın büyük çaba harcayarak bağırmasını ve ses çıkarmadaki yoğun uğraşını adlandırır. Tür ve çaba koşulları anlamın kurucu parçalarıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam karganın sesine ve bu sesi var gücüyle çıkarmasına özgüdür.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın kullanımı karşılar, fakat anlamı bütün yüksek seslere veya başka hayvan seslerine genişletmez.

concept_map.definition: Karganın sesini çıkarmak için büyük çaba harcayarak var gücüyle bağırmasıdır.

facets.statement: Sesi çıkaran kargadır ve ses güçlü bir bağırış biçimindedir.
Bağırış, yoğun çaba harcanarak ve var güçle çıkarılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, karganın bağırışını ve bu sesi çıkarmak için gösterdiği yoğun çabayı aynı anlamın parçaları olarak verir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Karganın güçlü ve çabalı ses çıkarmasını anlatan akıcı metinlerde kullanılabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bir hayvanın güçlü ve işitilir biçimde bağırmasını anlatır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Sesin kargadan çıkmasını ve yoğun çabayla üretilmesini gerektirir.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da yükseltilmiş, belirgin ve güçlü sesi kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal belirli bir hayvan türünün çıkardığı sesi adlandırır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, çakmak taşının ateşi hiç çıkarmamasını değil, onu yavaş ve güçlükle çıkarmasını anlatır. Yavaşlık, güçlük ve sonunda ateşin çıkması birlikte korunmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam yalnız çakmak taşı ile kurulan söz öbeğine ve gecikmiş ateş çıkarma olayına bağlıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnız çakmak taşının ateş çıkarmasıyla kurulan söz öbeğini kapsar; yalın biçime yaklaşma veya genel gecikme anlamı vermez.

concept_map.definition: Çakmak taşının ateşi hemen değil, yavaşça ve güçlükle çıkarmasıdır; gecikmeye rağmen ateş sonunda çıkar.

facets.statement: Çakmak taşı ateş çıkarır, ancak bu sonuç olağan hızda gerçekleşmez.
Ateşin çıkışı yavaş, gecikmeli ve güçlükle olur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, çakmak taşının ateşini yavaş ve güçlükle çıkarmasında birleşir; tam başarısızlık değil, gecikmiş çıkış söz konusudur.

concept_gloss.applicability: Çakmak taşının sonunda ateş çıkardığı, fakat bunun gecikmeli ve güç olduğu söz öbeğine uygundur.
